issues.failure_explanation: The introduction asserts, as a finding of the paper, that for the stochastic Schrödinger equation the data space spanned by the solution trajectory itself admits only polynomial-dimensional approximation. Subsection schrodinger proves only Proposition prop-dis, a logarithmic-dimension approximation of the averaged trajectory E[u(t)]; no result (not even an upper bound, let alone the needed lower bound) is established for the data space spanned by u(t) itself. The prose thus claims more than the formal content supports.

issues.overall_effect: The advertised intriguing contrast in the introduction and the contribution bullet about trajectory-dimension analysis for the stochastic Schrödinger equation overstate what is proved; readers are told a lower-bound-type fact that is never established.

issues.failure_explanation: The odd-order drift coefficients are extracted from E[Arg(ratio)], but Arg is only defined modulo 2π and the argument of the random ratio exp(A(ξ)Δt + c(ξ)ΔW) is wrapped by the Gaussian increment with positive probability for every fixed Δt>0; hence E[Arg_pv] differs from the displayed linear expression and identity (dri-mul-ide2) does not follow. The proof only asserts that the ambiguity 'can be removed' for small Δt, with no estimate of the wrapping bias. Moreover, uniqueness as stated is false without a branch/size hypothesis: shifting an odd coefficient, e.g. a_{e_j} -> a_{e_j} + 2π/Δt, changes A(ξ) by 2πi ξ_j/Δt, which leaves exp(A(ξ)Δt), and hence the two-time data on the integer Fourier grid, unchanged. Proposition prop:added-2 rebuilds b_β from the same pathwise Arg identities and inherits the same gap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose an explicit branch/smallness hypothesis (e.g., uniqueness restricted to coefficient sets with |Im A(ξ)|Δt < π on Q) and prove a Gaussian-tail bound showing the principal-value bias of E[Arg] is O(e^{-c/Δt}), yielding recovery of a_α up to an exponentially small error (or exact uniqueness within the principal branch); make the same fix in prop:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The exact uniqueness claim for the drift coefficients (odd-order terms, both noise cases) in Proposition prop-drift-identification, and the pathwise multiplicative result prop:added-2, are unsupported; the identifiability guarantee advertised for the drift step of Stoch-IDENT is weakened.

issues.failure_explanation: C^p regularity of a kernel does not imply eigenvalue decay λ_j = o(j^{-(p+1)}). Counterexample: G(s,t) = g(s−t) with g ∈ C^p whose Fourier coefficients satisfy ĝ(j) ≍ j^{-(p+3/4)} (such g exist, since g^{(p)} can be any nonzero H^{3/4} function); then λ_j = ĝ(j) and j^{p+1}λ_j = j^{1/4} → ∞, violating o(j^{-(p+1)}). The standard bound obtainable from C^p kernels is λ_j = O(j^{-p}), giving tail o(k^{−p+1}) and dimension O(ε^{−2/(p−1)}), not the claimed o(ε^{−2/p}); for p = 1 even the qualitative conclusion degenerates. The cited result is therefore applied outside any hypotheses established in the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Applying the left Riemann sum and Euler-Maruyama scheme 
to approximate the integral and stochastic integral respectively in~\eqref{eq_SPDE_integral_form} formally gives

u(t_i, x) - u(t_{i-1},x) = \sum_{k=1}^K
 a_k\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_i}F_k(t,x)\,dt +\sum_{j=1}^J b_j\int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_i} G_j(t,x)\,dW_t

issues.failure_explanation: For multiplicative noise the diffusion features are random, G_j = G_j(u), so the left-point Euler–Maruyama error ε_i = ∫ b_j G_j(u(t,x)) dW − b_j G_j(u(t_{i-1},x))ΔW has E|ε_i|² = ∫ E|G_j(u(t)) − G_j(u(t_{i-1}))|² dt = Θ(Δt²) (since E|u(t)−u(s)|² = O(|t−s|)), i.e. an L² error of order Δt, not Δt^{3/2}. Concretely, for du = u dW the one-step residual u(t_{i-1})(e^{ΔW−Δt/2} − 1 − ΔW) has second moment e^{Δt} − 1 − Δt ≈ Δt²/2. The claimed O(Δt^{3/2}) remainder is therefore false in the multiplicative regime (it holds only for deterministic/additive features). The downstream expectation relation (eq_deterministic_part) is unaffected because the Itô error has mean zero and the true expectation error is O(Δt²).

u(t_i, x) - u(t_{i-1},x) = \sum_{k=1}^K

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the remainder as O(Δt) in L²(Ω) for multiplicative features (keeping O(Δt^{3/2}) only for deterministic/additive features); this is a local re-labelling of the error bookkeeping with no change to the method or its guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed consistency rate of the discretized SPDE increment relation is overstated in the multiplicative case; the drift system (eq_linear_feature_system) remains valid since its true expectation-level error is smaller.
issues.title: Wrong discretization error rate for the Euler-Maruyama step
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the error bookkeeping preserves all downstream relations and the advertised performance, since the expectation-level relation actually holds with O(Δt²).

issues.failure_explanation: The pseudocode breaks only when the residual strictly increases; if an iteration reproduces the previous support and coefficient fit (possible, e.g., when Step 2's nonlinear regression returns the same j-sparse solution), then η^{(ℓ+1)} = η^{(ℓ)} and the loop repeats forever. The text states termination 'when the regression error does not improve', which contradicts the pseudocode that continues on non-improvement. Hence the output contract (I* with |I*| = j and coefficients ĉ* with supp(ĉ*) = I*) is not guaranteed for every input; no fallback or iteration cap is part of the algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the break test to non-improvement (use ≥ instead of >), or add a maximal-iteration rule that outputs the last iterate; one line, no change to the stated behavior on terminating runs.
issues.overall_effect: The input-output contract of Algorithm QSPalgo is not well defined for all inputs: on plateaus the procedure never returns the promised I*, ĉ*.
issues.title: QSP can fail to terminate on residual plateaus
issues.why_classification: A routine local fix restores well-definedness; all described behavior and empirical guarantees survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Define $\Psi_N:=\arg\min_{\bc\in\mathbb{R}^K}\{f_N(\bc): \|\bc\|_0=k\}$ and $\Psi_O:=\arg\min_{\bc\in\mathbb{R}^K}\{f_O(\bc): \|\bc\|_0=k\}$
The optimal value of~\eqref{eq_L0_drift_select_greedy} converges almost surely to the optimal value of~\eqref{eq_L0_drift_select_sample}.

issues.failure_explanation: The feasible sets of the constrained problems are {‖c‖_0 = k}, a finite union of punctured low-dimensional subspaces, which is neither closed nor the set C_k = {c : ‖c‖ = k} (Euclidean sphere) used in the proof; epi-convergence on the sphere cannot deliver the stated conclusions about ℓ0-constrained optimal values and Kuratowski–Mosco limits of argmin sets. Additionally, item 1 states the convergence direction in reverse (the sample problem's optimal value converges to the deterministic one, not conversely). The conclusions are in fact true—they follow from the a.s. entrywise convergence of (F^N, y^N), which yields uniform convergence of f_N to f_O on bounded sets plus attainment of the minima—so the defect is confined to the written argument.

failure_location.quote: Since $\bc^*$  is a local minimizer of $f_O$, by Theorem 5.1 of~\cite{vogel1994stochastic}, $f_N$ is lower semi-continuously convergent almost surely  to $f_O$ on the set $C_k := \{\bc:\|\bc\|=k\}$ (See Definition 2.6~\cite{vogel1994stochastic}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invocation by a direct epi-convergence argument on the closed set {‖c‖_0 ≤ k} (uniform a.s. convergence on compacts of f_N to f_O from entrywise SLLN, plus attainment), and reverse the direction in item 1; the same route then supplies the diffusion analogue.
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic guarantees for the sample-average approximations (both drift and, via the 'similarly deduced' diffusion theorem) rest on an inapplicable citation and a reversed convergence statement; the convergence claims are unsupported as written.
issues.title: SAA convergence proved on the wrong constraint set
issues.why_classification: A routine, contained repair (standard epi-convergence argument plus a direction typo) preserves both stated conclusions unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For any significance level p* ≤ 1/2 the critical value Φ^{-1}(p*) is negative, so the rule 'multiplicative if 2|Z_N| ≥ Φ^{-1}(p*)' fires for every data outcome and the procedure always declares multiplicative noise, contradicting its stated level-p* semantics. For p* > 1/2 the two thresholds are inconsistent and leave the region Φ^{-1}(p*)/2 ≤ 2|Z_N| < Φ^{-1}(p*) with no decision. A two-sided level-p* test on the standard-normal statistic Z_N thresholds |Z_N| at Φ^{-1}(1−p*/2); the stated thresholds (with the extra factors 2 and 1/2) do not implement the claimed false-positive-rate control.

failure_location.quote: Then for some significance level $p^* \in (0,1)$, we decide that the diffusion part contains multiplicative noise if $2|Z_N|\geq \Phi^{-1}(p^*)$, and it is only additive if $2|Z_N|<\Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two thresholds by the standard two-sided rule (declare multiplicative noise iff |Z_N| ≥ Φ^{-1}(1−p*/2), otherwise additive); a one-line fix that preserves the pipeline and its efficiency claims.
issues.overall_effect: The noise-type detection step, which decides whether the diffusion-identification pipeline is executed, does not deliver the stated error control and can leave outcomes unclassified.
issues.title: Additive-noise detection rule incomplete and mis-levelled
issues.why_classification: A local, routine correction of the decision rule preserves the method, its computational savings, and all downstream guarantees.
